title: Lindbladian quantum chaos beyond classical strange attractors
abstract: We investigate the connection between classical and quantum chaos in a dissipative system of two coupled collective spins. Although the classical dynamics possesses a stable fixed-point attractor, we find pronounced signatures of chaos in the transient dynamics preceding relaxation. In the quantum model, such transient chaos is accompanied by a transition to random-matrix statistics in the relevant part of the Liouvillian spectrum and by a qualitative increase in the number of Liouvillian modes contributing to expectation values of physical observables. The transition occurs before the bifurcation at which the stable fixed point disappears and a chaotic attractor emerges. Our results show that Liouvillian quantum chaos can be associated with transient classical chaos, rather than requiring a chaotic asymptotic attractor, and provide a refinement of the Grobe-Haake-Sommers conjecture.
summary: This paper examines chaos in an open quantum system of coupled spins, linking classical dynamics to quantum spectral properties. It demonstrates that quantum signatures of chaos, such as random-matrix statistics, can appear during the transient approach to a stable fixed point, rather than requiring the classical system to possess a fully chaotic attractor. This refines existing conjectures regarding quantum-classical correspondence in dissipative environments.
main_problem: The paper investigates the connection between classical and quantum chaos in a dissipative system, specifically exploring if quantum chaos signatures can arise from transient classical chaos rather than requiring a fully chaotic asymptotic attractor.
main_result: Liouvillian quantum chaos can be associated with transient classical chaos, suggesting a refinement of the Grobe–Haake–Sommers conjecture.
method: The study employs both classical stability analysis (analyzing fixed points and relaxation times) and quantum spectral analysis (diagonalizing the Liouvillian superoperator and examining spectral statistics).
model_or_system: The system is a quantum many-body model of two coupled collective spins, whose dynamics are governed by a Lindblad master equation. The classical limit is obtained by analyzing the expectation values of the spin operators.
key_observables: Liouvillian spectrum (eigenvalues), random-matrix statistics ($ho_{\lambda}$), expectation values of physical observables, and the standard deviations of the relaxation time ($\sigma_{ho}, \sigma_{\epsilon}$).
important_parameters: The dissipation strength ($\Gamma$) relative to a critical bifurcation point ($\Gamma_c$), and the initial distance from the fixed point ($\delta_{	ext{initial}}$).
main_assumptions: The classical analysis relies on the mean-field approximation, and the quantum analysis focuses on restricting spectral statistics to regions with significant observable expectation values.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of magnetization for both chaotic and stable regimes, and show the dependence of spectral statistics and the number of contributing eigenmodes on the dissipation strength $\Gamma$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the classical dynamics and identifying regimes (chaotic vs. stable fixed point). It then maps these classical behaviors onto quantum diagnostics, showing the emergence of random-matrix statistics and changes in observable expectation values in the Liouvillian spectrum, particularly in the transient regime.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the quantum-classical correspondence in open quantum systems, providing a mechanism to detect quantum chaotic signatures even when the classical dynamics settle into a stable, non-chaotic steady state.
